title: Variational preparation of thermofield double states for SYK models via multi-angle QAOA: sequential angle pruning for circuit reduction
authors: Haji Muhammad Husnain Ashfaq, Moongul Byun, Keun-Young Kim
abstract: Variational preparation of thermofield double (TFD) states can require deep quantum circuits, particularly for interacting many-body systems. Reducing these circuits while retaining high fidelity is therefore crucial for TFD-state preparation on noisy quantum processors. We study this problem by applying the multi-angle quantum approximate optimization algorithm (ma-QAOA) to TFD-state preparation and introducing two top-down sequential angle-pruning algorithms. Starting from the optimized initial ma-QAOA circuit, both algorithms sequentially remove Pauli-string evolutions with small optimized angles and reoptimize the remaining parameters after each removal. We apply these algorithms to Gaussian and binary Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) models in both dense and sparse cases. We find that ma-QAOA prepares the target TFD states with high fidelity and that sequential small-angle pruning retains high fidelity while reducing the circuit depth, particularly at low temperature. Moreover, using the post-reoptimization cost in sequential small-angle pruning further improves the fidelity. For the binary sparse $N=10$ SYK model at $β=10$, $88.8\%$--$92.1\%$ of the nonlocal Pauli-string evolutions are removed while retaining an average fidelity of approximately $95\%$. Finally, we propose extensions of the sequential pruning algorithms toward quantum--classical hybrid implementation.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of preparing complex Thermofield Double states for SYK models using deep quantum circuits. The authors introduce and test sequential angle-pruning algorithms applied to the multi-angle QAOA ansatz. These methods significantly reduce circuit depth while maintaining high fidelity, demonstrating a practical pathway toward implementing quantum simulations on near-term noisy quantum hardware.
main_problem: The primary challenge is preparing Thermofield Double (TFD) states using quantum circuits that are deep and resource-intensive, necessitating effective circuit reduction while maintaining high fidelity.
main_result: The proposed sequential angle-pruning algorithms (SAP/OSAP) successfully reduce the circuit depth by removing a large fraction of Pauli-string evolutions (up to 92.1%) while retaining an average fidelity near 95% for SYK models.
method: The study employs the multi-angle QAOA (ma-QAOA) ansatz to approximate the TFD state, followed by two top-down sequential angle-pruning techniques that iteratively remove the least significant Pauli-string evolutions and reoptimize the remaining parameters.
model_or_system: The work is applied to Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models, tested in both Gaussian and binary forms, across dense and sparse connectivity regimes. The TFD state is the target state, relevant for simulating quantum phenomena in holographic duality.
key_observables: Fidelity of the prepared TFD state, circuit depth (number of gates/blocks), and the percentage of removed nonlocal Pauli-string evolutions.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), number of qubits ($N$), and the pruning strength/candidate pool size ($S, N_C$).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that removing Pauli-string evolutions with small optimized angles does not significantly degrade the fidelity of the target TFD state, provided reoptimization is performed.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the SYK models and the pruning procedures (SAP-ma-QAOA and OSAP-ma-QAOA). Other figures track infidelity trajectories as a function of pruning strength or candidate pool size.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for circuit reduction in TFD state preparation, introduces ma-QAOA, and then details the two sequential angle-pruning algorithms (SAP and OSAP). The methods are validated by applying them to various SYK models, comparing fidelity retention against circuit depth reduction.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the resource limitations of quantum computation by developing systematic, data-driven methods to compress variational quantum circuits used for simulating complex many-body physics models like SYK.
